definitions.explanation: Describes a road or surface that has not been paved with asphalt or concrete. The prefix 未～ indicates something not yet done.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{未舗装|みほそう}だ。
{未舗装|みほそう}の{道路|どうろ}は{雨|あめ}の{後|あと}ぬかるみやすい。
examples.english: Unpaved roads tend to get muddy after rain.

examples.japanese: {山奥|やまおく}には{未舗装|みほそう}の{林道|りんどう}がまだ{多|おお}く{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There are still many unpaved forest roads deep in the mountains.

notes:
A compound of the prefix {未|み}～ (not yet) and {舗装|ほそう} (paving). Used as a no-adjective to describe roads or surfaces that have not been paved.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {未舗装|みほそう}の{道|みち}: unpaved road (no-adjective + の)
- {未舗装|みほそう}だ: is unpaved (predicate)

THE {未|み}～ PREFIX:
This prefix attaches to Sino-Japanese words to mean "not yet":
- {未完成|みかんせい}: incomplete
- {未経験|みけいけん}: inexperienced
- {未確認|みかくにん}: unconfirmed
- {未使用|みしよう}: unused

RELATED WORDS:
- {舗装|ほそう}: paving — the base word
- {砂利道|じゃりみち}: gravel road
- {土道|つちみち}: dirt road
- アスファルト: asphalt
